what: Server-side split of POST /approve on the deployed API before the latency fix, one fresh visitor per call, read from the response fields elapsed_ms (whole approve) and forecast.latency_ms (the re-forecast alone). Hand-transcribed from curl on 12 Oct 2026; there is no harness output file.

local_reference.where: laptop, stub backend, FastAPI TestClient, fresh sandbox
local_reference.before_fix: approve 1.5 s for both plays, forecast 0.5 s (so the live forecast ran about 5x slower than the laptop)
local_reference.after_fix: approve 0.4 s for both plays, forecast 0.2 s

reading: The same play ranged from 7.0 to 13.4 s on identical inputs while the forecast stayed at 2.5 s, so the variable part is the BigQuery copy branch. google-cloud-bigquery applies result(timeout=) per HTTP request and its default job_retry re-submits the query on backend and rate-limit errors, so the 6 s timeout did not cap that branch. The fixed floor (about 7 s) is local CPU work that ran in front of the copy call.
caveat: Four samples, one afternoon, a scale-to-zero service shared with other sessions. The Cloud Run logs for the warning 'copy generation via BigQuery AI.GENERATE_TABLE failed' were not readable from this machine; they would show how often the copy call fails or exceeds its budget.
